newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends bourse trade at new record high.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends bourse trade at new record high.

text.p: Germany's blue-chip DAX index ended bourse trade at a new closing high on Monday with sentiment lifted by Friday's strong close on Wall Street above 7,000 points, firmer debt and a stable, if lower, dollar.
At the end of the floor-trade session the DAX index stood at 3,436.07 points, up 59.87 points or 1.77 percent, an all-time closing high for the index.
The DAX later ended IBIS trade up 7.26 points at 3,426.77 points.

Among the main gainers on Monday was engineering group Deutz AG, which was continuing to enjoy positive sentiment after reports last week that the group would report a profit next year. Deutz ended up 14.18 percent at 12 marks.
Monday was also the opening day for trade in Frankfurt's new market for technology, new media and other growth stocks, the Neue Markt, modelled on New York's Nasdaq index.

The initial public offering in shares in German mobile phone service provider Mobilcom AG, which will trade on the Neue Markt, were more than 100 times oversubscribed, its chief executive Gerhard Schmid told Reuters on Monday.
Also due for a listing on the Neue Markt on Monday was the engineering services company Bertrandt AG.
The share market was gearing up for a rash of corporate information this week, with the three big chemical companies all due to report this week and next week.
Results for 1996 are due on Tuesday from Hoechst AG and Bayer AG, while the other member of the triumvirate of German chemical giant, BASF AG, will report its figures next week.
Shares in all three companies were strongly favoured over bourse trade.
Bayer ended up 4.35 marks at 77 marks, BASF ended up 2.51 marks at 66.15 marks and Hoechst AG ended up 21.70 marks at 79.50 marks.
Henkel KGaA shares ended floor trade up 40 pfennigs at 99.60 marks, well off earlier highs, after it reported a stronger 1996 dividend and forecast positive business developments in 1997.
